title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Gymnast Reuben Ward goes from Glasgow dreamer to Scotland gold medallist
description: There was a sense beforehand that Ward could contend here. A bronze maybe. Perhaps even a silver depending how things go. His team-mates privately mad
body: There was a sense beforehand that Ward could contend here. A bronze maybe. Perhaps even a silver depending how things go. His team-mates privately made noises that, should everything fall in his favour, gold could be within reach. They had seen him in training, and performed alongside him in the team event on Friday, where Scotland finished fourth. They knew he was in a good place.Ward sat seventh after the floor exercise, but streaked into the lead after a splendid performance on the pommel - routinely his strongest event. He retained that advantage after the rings - by which point assorted Team Scotland officials and members of the Scottish media had arrived in dribs and drabs, with the sniff of a gold in the air.Ward's vault had been compromised in the team event by a slight issue in his run up - he had to adapt it on the fly and could only execute two twists - but he nailed it this time, performing three to go into the final two rotations top of the standings.A strong showing in the parallel bars - and a judicious Team Scotland appeal to add an extra 0.100 - maintained his lead at 0.550, meaning he needed to keep his shape in the horizontal bar to clinch gold.Ward did that and more. As he stuck his landing, his coach Jake Seager fell to his knees celebrating before the two embraced. It wasn't official yet, but they knew."I like to imagine the best scenario possible and that was winning," added Ward when asked what he was thinking as his head hit the pillow on Saturday night."It kept me awake a little bit because I was picturing it and feeling the emotions. But this beat the expectations by a mile. "Falling short on Friday was heartbreaking and I'm just so overwhelmed, man. I can barely put words together."It could get even better. He goes on the floor and pommel on Monday, and is a real medal contender in the later.His celebrations will have to wait for now, but by Tuesday, Ward could well be getting up to all sorts of capers in Glasgow with his Scotland team-mates."Tonight looks like eating hotel food and probably getting a pretty bad night's sleep," he said. "Then I'll come in tomorrow, and try to relax and hit my routine. "On Tuesday, after the competition, I'll celebrate big time with the team, with my boys. I love them so much and them coming to see me at the end when I was going around of the arena was special."I'm hoping we'll get to experience a bit of Glasgow.. "

schema.headline: Commonwealth Games 2026: Gymnast Reuben Ward goes from Glasgow dreamer to Scotland gold medallist

title: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'
description: Image caption, Andy Burnham spoke exclusively to Laura Kuenssberg this week in his first major interview as prime minister BySunday with Laura Kuenssb
body: Image caption, Andy Burnham spoke exclusively to Laura Kuenssberg this week in his first major interview as prime minister BySunday with Laura KuenssbergAndy Burnham says he would be prepared to call out Donald Trump to defend Britain's "national interest before anything else" if it is the right thing to do, in his first major interview as prime minister.Speaking exclusively to the BBC, Burnham said he had had a good first exchange with Trump, finding him to be "really warm".But asked twice if he would trust the US president, he did not say, answering, "it's a changing world isn't it, and you just obviously have to call things as they develop".In the interview, to be broadcast in full on Monday, he said: "I can't at any point say that I won't take a different opinion from him [Trump], that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain."Figure caption, Watch: 'You have to defend your own national interest before anything else'Burnham said: "My strength is remaining close to people, close to the public, that will not change as prime minister."Asked if he would call out Trump if it was the right thing, he said, "of course", going on to say: "You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly."Burnham also said he had had "concern" about the president starting the conflict with Iran, and he "wouldn't hold back from saying what I think is right".Responding to Burnham's comments, Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: "Clearly, the US is a long standing ally. We need to have good relations with them but if they do something we disagree with, we should honestly say so."The prime minister would not commit to a date when the government would spend 3% of GDP on defence. His Chancellor John Healey resigned from the previous government saying that unless a commitment was made to spend that amount by 2030, the country would not be safe.But Burnham said: "I appointed my new chancellor very aware of what he had said about the critical importance of defence spending and the position that he had taken about that."The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded and that's the thing that's right in front of us and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year."Figure caption, Watch: PM says 'we've got to work out the way' of meeting defence promisesAsked again specifically about the commitment to increase defence spending to 3% of GDP, he said: "We've got to work out the way of doing that."Burnham, for the first time, explicitly dismissed the idea of an early general election before 2029, saying: "I'm going to rule it out... I don't think people want it." He said his focus instead was on "getting the country back where it should be".Philp said the Conservatives were ready to fight an election whenever it happens."It pretty clear to me we are back in business and that the polls suggest that we are pretty much neck and neck with other parties" he said.Watch the full interview, BBC Panorama 'Andy Burnham: the Laura Kuenssberg Interview' on iPlayer from 06:00 on Monday and BBC One on Monday at 20:00 BST.

schema.headline: Burnham says he is prepared to call out Trump 'if right for Britain'

title: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider
description: Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the company has announced.Speaking duri
body: Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the company has announced.Speaking during the surprise announcement at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday, Gosling said it is a character he has "wanted to play for a very long time".The film is due to be released in 2028, and will be the third about the motorcycle-riding anti-hero.It will follow the 2007 film of the same name starring Nicolas Cage, and its follow-up, 2011's Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.Before making the big reveal on stage at San Diego Comic-Con, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said he had often been asked when Gosling would join the MCU.Shortly after, the lights turned off. When they returned, the actor appeared on stage to cheers from screaming fans.Speaking about the role, Gosling said: "Wow, is this really happening?"He has previously spoken about his desire to take on the role. Appearing on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast in March, he confirmed he was in discussions with Marvel.Ghost Rider is the anti-hero identity of motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze.The character's story begins when he becomes bound to the Spirit of Vengeance Zarathos after making a deal with villain Mephisto to spare his surrogate father, giving him superpowers.The film will be directed by Shawn Levy, who Gosling described as the "only" director for the project.Levy has previously directed Deadpool & Wolverine in the MCU, and is currently working with Gosling on Star Wars: Starfighter, which is due to be released next year.Levy told the crowd that he and Gosling spent a lot of their downtime on set daydreaming about Ghost Rider and swapping ideas.The director said: "As Ryan started talking about his vision for this character, we started riffing, and I finally said, 'bro, let's ride', so guys, we'll see you in 2028."

schema.headline: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider

title: Prince of Wales boat tragedy that killed 15 remembered 60 years on
description: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned fromImage caption, Peter Watts was just 14-years-old when he lost his mother, father, br
body: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned fromImage caption, Peter Watts was just 14-years-old when he lost his mother, father, brother and sister in the boating disasterByGeorge HerdBBC Wales"It's something you don't get over - you learn to live with it."Sixty years ago, Peter Watts' entire family was killed in a boating tragedy that shocked the nation.His nine-year-old sister Angela, 10-year-old brother David, mother Doreen and father Frederick George, along with 11 others, died when the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank on the Mawddach Estuary in Gwynedd on 22 July, 1966.Now, a memorial recalling the names of the 15 people who lost their lives has been unveiled.It was another chance for Peter to travel from the village he grew up in, near Milton Keynes, to the picturesque estuary where the catastrophe unfolded.Image source, Mirrorpix via Getty ImagesImage caption, Divers search for remaining survivors on the Mawddach Estuary back in July 1966 after the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank"We'd been on holidays in previous years and I'd been on this boat trip [before] and I didn't want to go again," Peter recalled.Peter was 14 at the time, old enough to be allowed to spend the day on his own in the seaside town of Barmouth, where his family were staying in a boarding house.The rest of his family joined the queue to board the Prince of Wales for the eight mile (13km) trip down the estuary to the George III Hotel at Penmaenpool.Image source, Peter WattsImage caption, Peter's parents Doreen and Frederick George, seen here on their wedding day, died in the tragedyBut the tide pushed the ferry boat into the Penmaenpool toll bridge across the estuary, flinging the 42 passengers into the water as the vessel was wrecked on the bridge.Local people, including the hotel owner and staff and the toll bridge keeper, ran to the aid of those in the water, managing to pull 27 to safety.But along with Peter's brother and sister, two other children were among the 15 who could not be saved.Image source, Mirrorpix via Getty ImagesImage caption, The tragedy led to changes in the law on the number of passengers boats such as the Prince of Wales could carry"This happened in the morning, at about 11 in the morning, and I was just waiting hours and hours for them to come back - and they didn't come back," said Peter."I went down to the harbour and I heard two people talking about a boat that had sunk. I asked them what was going on, and they said what it was, and I said 'My family is on it' - and they said 'Go to the police station'."I sat in there for what seemed ever and a day, and they took the details."The guest house owners came to take him back, while his aunt and uncle drove up to be with him."The next morning we went to Dolgellau to the hospital, where they had found three of them - my mother was still missing," he said."My father could swim, but my uncle who identified him said he had had a nasty blow on his head."It would be another three days before his mother's body was found.Image source, Peter WattsImage caption, This picture of Peter's brother and sister, David, 10, and Angela, nine, was taken only a few weeks before the disasterAn official inquiry found the boat was carrying six more passengers than the maximum 36 permitted under its certification.There should also have been two crew members - one on the engine and one on the rudder.But there was only skipper Edward Llewelyn, 73 at the time, who was found to have acted negligently by a Board of Trade inquiry.The boat was also short of lifebelts and buoyancy apparatus was stowed away.Llewelyn was ordered to pay £100 towards the inquiry costs, but no prosecutions were ever brought.However, the inquiry did lead to changes in the law governing insurance and the number of passengers boats could carry.Image caption, A new memorial to the tragedy names each of the victims, including Peter's familyThe events have left a deep mark on Peter, and the urge to return to Barmouth and the estuary as often as he could."If I've ever been anywhere near Wales, even when I've been going to Holyhead, when we went to Ireland, I'd come round this way," he said."Just to spend a few minutes."Returning this time on the 60th anniversary of the tragedy, it was marked with a special memorial and the plaque to remember those who died, unveiled by Dolgellau Town Council."Those 15 people - I didn't want them to be forgotten. Having their names there - that's what I wanted," said Peter.

schema.headline: Prince of Wales boat tragedy that killed 15 remembered 60 years on

title: Meghan calls Prince Harry 'a charmer' during MasterChef Australia appearance
description: Early on in the episode, Meghan was asked what her favourite dish is to make at home.She said it was "a tough one because I have a lot of palettes to
body: Early on in the episode, Meghan was asked what her favourite dish is to make at home.She said it was "a tough one because I have a lot of palettes to appease", with her British-born husband favouring "meat, potatoes and cream sauce" while she preferred grilled fish.Their two children, Archie and Lilibet, often help with meal preparation and are "great eaters", she said."We're really lucky on that front," she added.She then urged the chefs to cook something they felt connected to. "What's the story behind it?" she asked them.When Prince Harry dialled in later on during the episode, Meghan told them: "My husband's here," prompting cheers and shocked faces from contestants and spectators."I wish you could try these, these dishes are fantastic," she told him, before showing him the food. He signed off by telling her to go and enjoy, adding: "Very sorry to disturb you."The duchess’s appearance on the latest season of the show was well received by Hello Magazine, external, which shared a video of the episode online and complimented Meghan for the way she interacted with the chefs."The Duchess of Sussex gave personal time calls to all the contestants, proving that she's always so effortlessly elegant," it wrote.Writing in The Sunday Times, external, Charlotte Ivers was less impressed, saying her appearance on the show "told us nothing about what she likes or who even will leave the competition".Social media users were also split, with one viewer writing that Meghan was "warm, gracious and a delight to watch" while another called Prince Harry's cameo appearance "cringe".

schema.headline: Meghan calls Prince Harry 'a charmer' during MasterChef Australia appearance

title: Hungarian Grand Prix result: Lando Norris wins from Max Verstappen with Kimi Antonelli third
description: Lando Norris took his and McLaren's first grand prix victory of the year in a compelling race in Hungary.As the world champion cruised to a comfortabl
body: Lando Norris took his and McLaren's first grand prix victory of the year in a compelling race in Hungary.As the world champion cruised to a comfortable victory, there was a tense fight for the remaining podium positions in the closing laps between Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli.Verstappen just managed to hold on while Antonelli took third to extend his championship lead to 50 points over Lewis Hamilton and 59 over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who finished seventh after a bad start.Ferrari's Hamilton finished the grand prix on Antonelli's tail in fourth place but was penalised five seconds for speeding in the pit lane and dropped to fifth behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc.Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri led for most of the first half of the race but retired from second place with a gearbox failure.Norris said he was "happy to be back and be number one again", adding: "My pace today was probably some of the best pace I've ever had. The car was beautiful to drive and I had confidence."The key stories of the race were:Norris' victory, helped by a controversial strategy that did not please his team-mate PiastriA surprise second for Verstappen after a strategy gamble paid off for Red BullYet another penalty harming Hamilton's prospects in a disappointing race for Ferrari given their paceA positive weekend for Aston Martin with their new car, despite not scoring pointsNorris' concern before the start would have been about the losing a place to Leclerc, who was starting second behind the Briton.The McLaren driver made a good start, the challenge from Leclerc never materialised, but instead Norris lost the lead to Piastri.Norris was leading through Turn Two, but a strong start put the Australian second, and when Norris made an error and ran wide through Turn Two, Piastri seized his opportunity to take the lead.That left McLaren with a quandary for although their cars were running one-two, the slower one was in the lead, and they were concerned about threats from behind.Piastri led through the first pit stops, with Norris never much more than a second behind, but Norris started to challenge hard in the second stint and wanted to be given the opportunity to challenge his team-mate.Norris asked to make his second stop first but was refused.Instead, Piastri was called in, McLaren saying they were covering the threat from Hamilton, who had just stopped himself, and Norris was allowed to run for six further laps before making his pit call for fresh tyres.Norris returned to the track just in front of Piastri, who had been delayed by a collision with Williams driver Carlos Sainz while lapping the Spaniard, who was penalised five seconds for the incident.Piastri was clearly unhappy, telling his engineer not to talk to him shortly after Norris returned to the track.But Norris' pace afterwards justified the decision and he pulled away into a comfortable lead.Piastri had just been promoted back to second place by Antonelli's second pit stop when he lost use of his gearbox on lap 56 and pulled off after Turn Three.That led to a late virtual safety car (VSC) which enlivened the battles behind Norris, but he was untouchable as he and McLaren, who came to Hungary with an upgraded car, revived memories of some of their dominant victories of their championship last year.Verstappen was unhappy with his car for much of the race, with regular complaints on team radio, but Red Bull pulled a masterstroke when they fitted soft tyres to his car at his second pit stop.The aim was to challenge Hamilton in the later laps after the seven-time champion made an early second stop with 40 laps still to go.It was heading towards a tense climax when Piastri's retirement brought out the VSC.That prompted a late round of pit stops, Ferrari bringing in both their drivers and putting them behind Verstappen.Hamilton came out of the pits and passed Antonelli into the first corner, after the Italian stayed out under the VSC, but had to give the place back after the restart because the Mercedes driver had just passed the key line on the track in front.Antonelli and Hamilton started chasing back towards Verstappen, but they were delayed while lapping Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.That looked as if it might be decisive, but in the end Verstappen was comfortably able to keep Antonelli at bay, crossing the line 3.6 seconds ahead.Another key point in Verstappen's race had been his re-passing of Hamilton after the Ferrari had got briefly ahead following the first pit stops.That gave him clear air and enabled the Dutchman to consolidate his race position in third place behind the McLarens, laying the foundations for Red Bull's late strategy call.Hamilton will leave Hungary ruing another penalty - the one for speeding in the pit lane was his second in two days after behind penalised for blocking Piastri in qualifying, and follows two others at the previous two races in Belgium and Britain.Behind him, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, ahead of Russell, who dropped to 21st place on the first lap after his anti-stall kicked in at the start, and fought back strongly.At Aston Martin, Lance Stroll finished in 13th, ahead of team-mate Fernando Alonso, their positions dictated to a degree by luck under the VSC and their divergent strategies.But the key point was that Alonso, in particular, was able to fight with other cars for the first time, and he ran a long first stint on the soft tyres, before switching to the mediums, which was a bold strategy.The long-awaited upgrade to their car, which was new apart from the front suspension, engine and gearbox, has reduced their lap times by about two seconds.A Honda engine upgrade is due for the Dutch Grand Prix, the next race in four weeks' time after the summer break, which the team hope will elevate them further and potentially bring the possibility of the occasional points finish into the picture.

schema.headline: Hungarian Grand Prix result: Lando Norris wins from Max Verstappen with Kimi Antonelli third

title: Teenager charged over record Channel crossing on 'mega dinghy'
description: A teenager charged over a small boat Channel crossing was allegedly piloting a "mega dinghy" carrying a record 165 migrants from France to England, th
body: A teenager charged over a small boat Channel crossing was allegedly piloting a "mega dinghy" carrying a record 165 migrants from France to England, the National Crime Agency has said.Sudanese national Chan Mathok Atak, 19, is accused of endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK on Thursday and is due to appear at Margate Magistrates' Court on Monday.The number on the dinghy broke the previous record from July, when 128 crossed the Channel from France on one vessel.According to Home Office figures, more than 13,000 arrivals have been recorded in 2026, which is 45% lower than this time in 2025 and down 18% on the same period in 2024.Border Security Command was pictured towing a dinghy - estimated to be about the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover in Kent on Thursday afternoon.Home Office figures showed 366 people arrived after crossing in three boats on Thursday during warm, sunny weather and calm conditions at sea.On Wednesday, 172 people made the journey in three boats, bringing an end to an 11-day hiatus because of windy conditions in the Channel.Refugee charity Care4Calais said the crossing route was becoming "more and more dangerous" because of the increasing number of people in each boat.

schema.headline: Teenager charged over record Channel crossing on 'mega dinghy'

title: Rental searches for pet friendly properties drop after law change
description: Image source, Getty ImagesByCost of living correspondentRightmove searches for rental properties that allow pets have plummeted since law changes gave
body: Image source, Getty ImagesByCost of living correspondentRightmove searches for rental properties that allow pets have plummeted since law changes gave renters more rights.Following the introduction of the new rules, pet searches dropped by more than 50% in May and June compared with a year earlier.Landlords in England cannot unreasonably refuse pets in their properties under changes made in May in the Renters' Rights Act.But agents say some renters wrongly believe permission to have a pet is guaranteed, and landlords say some homes remain unsuitable for multiple pets or large dogs."Landlords must consider requests fairly and cannot unreasonably refuse them, but they can still decline where there is a valid reason," said Megan Eighteen, former president of lettings agents trade body ARLA Propertymark.She said there was plenty of "potential for misunderstanding", among tenants about pet-friendly properties.Power shift over petsThe Rightmove data suggests that fewer tenants are proactively filtering for pet-friendly properties when searching for a home. While pets remain the most common searched-for term overall - ahead of gardens, garages and furnishings, the lead at the top is shrinking.Renter searches for properties that allow pets fell by 54% in May and 52% in June compared with the same months a year earlier, according to the figures shared with the BBC. Falls had accelerated through this year, as the changes got closer and were then introduced.Marc von Grundherr, director of agency Benham and Reeves, said some tenants have only disclosed a pet after signing their tenancy agreement, while others have been discovered during property inspections."The reality is that tenants now understand the balance of power has shifted. Landlords can no longer rely on a blanket 'no pets' policy to deter applications and should instead expect conversations around pet ownership to arise much later in the letting process," he said.Now, in England, landlords may still be able to refuse a pet if another tenant has an allergy, the property is too small for a large pet or several pets, the pet is illegal, or the landlord is a leaseholder and the freeholder does not allow pets.Before the rules changed, Eve Williamson had to give up her American Bulldog, Khan, or face eviction from her home - despite having previously had a dog in the property.The 41-year-old former hairdresser, from London, described the experience as awful, especially as Khan had brought comfort while she gave full-time care to her mum."Life can get tough, but pets bring unconditional love," she said. "They're family."Image source, Eve WilliamsonImage caption, Eve had to give up her dog - Khan - or face evictionKhan has since been happily re-homed, and Eve said she was delighted with the law change. Katie Smith, 29, from Swindon, has two cats - Pumpkin and Pippin - in her rental home. The new mum said the family had shared "wonderful moments" with pets, which would also teach children about life and death.But she said the choice of places to rent still dropped sharply on property portals when pets were part of the equation."Landlords should give them a chance," she said. Yet, even under the new rules, landlords were finding excuses to refuse potential tenants with pets, according to Russell Hunt, founder of Pets Lets, which matches clients with pet-friendly rentals.Image source, Russell HuntImage caption, Russell Hunt said landlords should consider each pet request on its meritsHe lives with a Basset Beagle cross, called Biscuit, and his three teenagers, who he jokes are more disruptive than the dog.He said pet CVs should be used and landlords should consider the circumstances more carefully, such as older dogs being calmer and sleeping more, rather than simply ruling out tenants with large or multiple pets. Cost to landlordsRepresentatives for landlords say they understand the importance of companionship that pets offer to tenants, but they can still face costly damage."Many landlords have legitimate concerns about the risk that some irresponsible pet owners pose to rental properties, or that some owners may try to keep pets in properties that are not appropriate for animals," said Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association.He said that landlords faced issues including: No power to compel tenants to take out insuranceNo legal right to request an additional depositA burden of costs should a pet cause damage to a propertyLesley Horton, the UK's chief property ombudsman said that landlords should not be levying pet surcharges as this fell outside permitted fees for issues such as late payments or lost key replacements.However, a landlord could make deductions from the tenancy deposit at the end of the tenancy for proven pet-related damage.Additional reporting by Kris Bramwell. Get in touchAre you affected by the issues raised in this story?

schema.headline: Rental searches for pet friendly properties drop after law change

title: Firefighters battle France wildfire as tens of thousands evacuated near Bordeaux
description: Firefighters are battling to contain wildfires burning near to the city of Bordeaux as tens of thousands of people have been evacuated from the surrou
body: Firefighters are battling to contain wildfires burning near to the city of Bordeaux as tens of thousands of people have been evacuated from the surrounding region. Speaking on Sunday, the city's Mayor, Thomas Cazenave, said the fire was about 15km (9 miles) from the outskirts of the city's wider region, and 25 to 30km (15 and 19 miles) from its centre, although downplayed the possibility of Bordeaux being evacuated. Overnight into Sunday about 55,000 people were evacuated from villages to the south of the city in the Gironde region, famed for its vineyards.  Wildfires have raged across Europe over the past week, primarily France and Spain, where more than 330,000 people have been evacuated. South-west France has been one of worst affected regions, with an area of 42,000 hectares burnt, making it one of the largest forest fires since World War Two. About 98,000 hectares have burnt across the country since the start of the year. In total, more than 220,000 people have been evacuated in the south west of the country. Captain Nicolas Braz, one of the leaders of the firefighting operation, said the fire had created "its own winds - complete with whirlwinds", adding it was "erratic and unmanageable".France's Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Sunday the situation in the region remained "very unfavourable" and the wildfire was "moving erratically towards the Bordeaux metropolitan area".In the Gironde region, the rescue effort involves 2,500 firefighters, including a Swiss team, 1,500 military personnel and almost 1,200 police and gendarmes, who are carrying out evacuations and helping with rescue and securing operationsDry vegetation and brisk winds are causing the fire to spread, with 60km (37 miles) of the A63 motorway, which leads to Spain, having been closed. On Sunday afternoon, Bordeaux Airport's departures and arrivals boards were showing delays to every flight from 17:15 onwards. Some 28 Easyjet flights alone were delayed, many with no new departure or arrival time given, and five cancelled including UK flights.Bordeaux Airport told BBC News air traffic control restrictions had been put in place "to facilitate the work of the emergency services" in fighting the fires, with all commercial flights affected. It is unclear how long the delays will last, the airport added.The final stage of the Tour de France, taking place in Paris on Sunday, has been shortened from 133km to 89km (from 82 miles to 55) to allow security forces to be redeployed to the firefighting effort.  President Emmanuel Macron said France would "rebuild" and his government would "be there for as long as is needed".Meanwhile in Spain, fires continue to spread, with more than 90,000 evacuated from the regions around Madrid and Ávila.Around 77,000 hectares have been affected by the fires in Spain, minister for ecological transition, Sara Aagesen, said on Sunday.She added that the wildfire burning in the Ávila region is the largest in the country's recent history.Overnight into Sunday, a new front also opened up near the coastal city of Valencia. Speaking to reporters late on Saturday, Valencia's regional President Juanfran Pérez Llorca, said: "The fire is beyond our capacity to extinguish."Pilar Bernabe, the central government's delegate to Valencia, said conditions in the region were likely to worsen throughout Sunday. Sunday is expected to bring high temperatures and low humidity, potentially allowing the fire to spread further. On Saturday, one civilian was killed in a smaller fire in the Valencia region - the only civilian death so far reported. Earlier in the week, two firefighters were killed fighting the blaze near to Bordeaux. Late on Saturday, at least eight municipalities near Toledo were also ordered to evacuate, though it was unclear how many people were involved.Speaking on Sunday during a visit to an area hit by wildfires to the west of Madrid, the country's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said "difficult hours lie ahead" but added there were "positive" indications overnight towards containing the blaze.He also said there needed to be "a major public pact on the climate emergency". Madrid's regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the situation as the "worst fire in the history of the region".

schema.headline: Firefighters battle France wildfire as tens of thousands evacuated near Bordeaux

title: Man in critical condition after sea rescue near Clacton-on-Sea
description: It follows a separate incident in West Mersea, near Colchester, on Wednesday in which a mother and her teenage daughter died. Shally Rahman, 41, and S
body: It follows a separate incident in West Mersea, near Colchester, on Wednesday in which a mother and her teenage daughter died. Shally Rahman, 41, and Samiha Rahman, 15, tried to help a seven-year-old relative out of the water. He remains in hospital in a critical condition.Ch Insp Stuart Austin, Clacton district commander, said: "I'm acutely aware there will be a sense of shock and worry given recent incidents elsewhere in north Essex in the last week."First and foremost, our thoughts are with those affected by the incident on the seafront yesterday. "I'm also aware the area was busy, and the incident would have been seen by a lot of people."Emergency services were quickly on the scene, and all services worked incredibly professionally to clear the area to allow for medical professionals to help the three people involved."He urged people not to comment about the incident on social media. title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars and farm land in West Bank, Palestinians say
description: Israeli settlers have set fire to two mosques, as well as cars and agricultural land in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say, as tensions
body: Israeli settlers have set fire to two mosques, as well as cars and agricultural land in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say, as tensions in the territory continue to flare. The latest attacks come two days after a clash between settlers and Palestinians near the village of Tal, which left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead.Both sides accused the other of provoking the violence. The confrontation has further inflamed the situation in the West Bank, which has seen ever growing violence by extremist settlers against Palestinians, encouraged by far-right elements in the current Israeli government.Palestinian reports say that two villages in the occupied West Bank came under attack from settlers overnight - with cars vandalised, property stolen and hate graffiti spray painted on walls.The mayor of Qusra said that settlers set fire to a mosque that was under construction.Abdul Azim Wadi said that settlers spray painted graffiti that included the word, "revenge", on the walls of the mosque.The Israeli military has said that troops were sent to Qusra and that police would investigate and collect evidence.Palestinian officials say that in a separate incident, settlers set fire to another mosque in the village of Kour and sprayed slogans on its walls.Since the deadly clash on Friday in Tal, Palestinians say that there have been multiple settler attacks on villages across the West Bank.The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has carried out raids and arrested dozens of Palestinians in what it's called a "counter-terrorism" operation.The Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded to the incident in Tal by vowing to take "powerful action".That includes the possible demolition of the homes of two of the Palestinians who were allegedly involved.There's been a sharp increase in settler attacks in the West Bank in recent months.It's drawn international condemnation, but has shown little or no sign of being reversed.The situation had already deteriorated before the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023.But since the subsequent war waged by Israel against Hamas in Gaza erupted, settler violence in the West Bank has escalated.The UN says 1,114 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank, the vast majority by the IDF. It says at least 35 of the deaths have involved attacks by settlers.It says 41 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war.Israel has built hundreds of settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them. The settlements are illegal under international law.

schema.headline: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars and farm land in West Bank, Palestinians say

title: Aitch on reaching new heights with his Mount Kilimanjaro climb
description: How rapper Aitch's sister inspired him to climb one of the world's toughest peaksImage source, Aaron FitzmauriceImage caption, The Manchester rapper h
body: How rapper Aitch's sister inspired him to climb one of the world's toughest peaksImage source, Aaron FitzmauriceImage caption, The Manchester rapper has been pursuing challenges to raise awareness and money for the Down's Syndrome AssociationByEleanor Doyle and Naomi ClarkeBBC NewsbeatHe's skydived, eaten raw fish eyes on I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! and now Aitch has reached new heights - literally - by climbing Mount Kilimanjaro.The Manchester rapper has been pursuing some of these tasks to raise awareness and money for the Down's Syndrome Association in honour of his younger sister Gracie, who has the condition. Aitch tells BBC Newsbeat the 16-year-old is an "absolute legend in the streets of Manchester" and beyond."Everyone loves her. She's just a big bottle of light in every room," he says."She's everyone's best friend and she's just got such a positive outlook on the world. "I just feel like everyone should be more like her."The musician's journey up Kilimanjaro has been captured in an upcoming Netflix documentary, Aitch: Don't Be Afraid.But he says the whole point of it was to share how having someone in his life with Down's syndrome is "one of the best things in the world".However, the 26-year-old admits he does feel "a little bit of pressure" to up the scale and fundraising targets of his challenges."You've just got to think about the end goal, which is trying to raise the most money and make the most difference to what's going on," he says.Image source, HandoutImage caption, Aitch says his sister Gracie is an "absolute legend in the streets of Manchester" and beyondHe has "smashed" his target this time by bringing in more than £160,000 so far from his climb of the highest peak in Africa. The rapper says he was able to handle the altitude and physical elements of the hike, which others in his group struggled with. But the "big mental challenge" was the biggest obstacle for him, he says.Between the early mornings, late nights and the change of climate from rainforest conditions one minute to a blizzard the next, Aitch says it was "just all a lot".He confesses the group would probably have turned around if they hadn't been doing the climb for "such a good cause".Down's syndrome is when you're born with an extra chromosome - and people with the condition are likely to have some level of learning disability.Aitch's fundraising efforts have been inspired by Gracie, who was also the subject of My G, a viral song he released in 2022. He thinks it was so popular because it showed the bond between the siblings."People love genuine things," he says."And that relationship there between me and my sister, both of my sisters, is just undeniable. Do you know what I'm saying? So I feel like that's why people loved it."Image source, Down’s Syndrome AssociationImage caption, The rapper's fundraising efforts have been inspired by Gracie, who was also the subject of his viral song My GHaving grown up as a sibling carer, Aitch has faced challenges, and seen Gracie overcome obstacles. Reflecting on how he would advise others in his position who are struggling, he says  "you've got to see the blessing in it every time". "I suppose if you ask yourself the question, 'would you change it for the world?', there's probably not a chance," he says."So it's always going to be a bit of a challenge, but sometimes you've got to just take it on the chin, keep it stepping and it'll all be all right."He also feels there is "always more that can be done" to support young carers and  improve understanding around various conditions and learning disabilities. "Where I stand, I'm trying to do what I do to raise awareness," he says. "And hopefully that brings people in. "Hopefully that makes people want to get a little bit more involved in the whole thing and just spread more awareness than ever." Aitch: Don't Be Afraid is available to stream on Netflix from 26 July. Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here.

title: What we know so far about the Berlin Pride ramming attack
description: Figure caption, Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attack as manhunt continuesUpdated 3 hours agoOne woman has been killed and at least 29 others inj
body: Figure caption, Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attack as manhunt continuesUpdated 3 hours agoOne woman has been killed and at least 29 others injured after a van was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night, in what officials say was likely an "Islamist terror attack".Police have launched an intensive manhunt for the suspect in the German capital. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has condemned the incident as a "heinous" attack. Here is what we know so far.  Follow live updatesWhat happened in the Berlin Pride attack?The attack happened at about 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT). A report was made to police in Berlin that a white vehicle had been driven into crowds at a Pride event in the capital. Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered at Tiergarten park, near the iconic Brandenburg Gate, for the annual event, which is known as Christopher Street Day. Some people were also stabbed in the incident, with a blade officials believe could have been a machete.Shortly afterwards, the Pride event was cancelled. A performance was abruptly brought to a end, with organisers taking to the stage and advising the crowd to start walking towards the exits. As the message was being given to the crowd, the word "evacuation" was projected onto a large screen on the stage. Unverified video posted to social media showed large crowds of people leaving the scene as emergency vehicles raced to the scene. At about 01:00 local time, police confirmed that one woman had been killed and many more had suffered injuries.A short time later, police confirmed they had found the vehicle believed to have been used in the attack, saying it had crashed into a tree. Image source, ReutersAt about 03:30, police said on X they had identified a suspect with Islamist links. No arrest has been made or motive suggested.The search area was widened to the entire city and involved thousands of police, including officers from surrounding German states.On Sunday, police officers stood guard outside an apartment block in Berlin's Tiergarten district, which is said to be the suspect's home. Who is the suspect in the Berlin Pride attack?The suspect has been named by police as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese background.He was known to police and has committed a number of crimes, officials said. He had previously been sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison, but the sentence was commuted to parole.Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the suspect had been radicalised. German media outlets are reporting he is a supporter of Islamic State group (IS), and tried in the past - unsuccessfully - to join the organisation.Police sources are quoted in German media as saying he travelled to Lebanon in 2025 and was arrested on his return to Berlin. Reports say he had been in pre-trial detention until May 2026 and had been ordered to take part in a de-radicalisation programme. He is believed to be connected to the vehicle found abandoned in the park. While his image has been released and a manhunt is under way, police have also said that one or more people may have fled the vehicle used, meaning there could be additional suspects. The police statement added that several people are reported to have been injured with stabbing weapons in the attack.Image source, Polizei BerlinPolice have called on members of the public to come forward with information, but have been warned not to engage with the suspect, who is believed to be armed and dangerous. At the time of the attack, Ballout, described as thin and around 6ft 2in, is believed to have been wearing a black hooded top and white trousers. Where did the attack happen?The attack took place in the popular Tiergarten park, near the Brandenberg Gate. A large number of people and floats took part in the Christopher Street Day event, which passed through the city, before moving through Tiergarten park, past the Victory Column monument, and towards the Brandenberg Gate. Berlin Police have said people were hit on Ahornsteig, which is a long path stretching across the park, largely in a forested area. European leaders have been swift to condemn the attack.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed her sympathy to the victims, saying the Pride event stands for "freedom, dignity, and equality - the fundamental values of the EU"."Every person should be able to live, love, and stand up for their rights without fear," she wrote on social media.Rob Jetten, prime minister of the Netherlands, said the Dutch stand "shoulder to shoulder with our German neighbours", while Italy's prime minister Georgia Meloni expressed "solidarity and sincere sympathy".The UK's defence secretary Wes Streeting called the incident "an absolutely horrific disaster", adding his thoughts and prayers are with the German people.Did you attend Berlin Pride? title: Emmerdale makers seek forever home for soap village in Leeds
description: The makers of TV drama Emmerdale hope to continue filming on their village set at  a site in Leeds after seeking permission from the council.ITV Studi
body: The makers of TV drama Emmerdale hope to continue filming on their village set at  a site in Leeds after seeking permission from the council.ITV Studios has applied to Leeds City Council to remain at the farm site in Harewood which the show has occupied since 1997.Current planning permission allows for the location, which includes the Woolpack pub and Burden Head Farm, to be used until next year.If granted, consent from council planners would allow the site, which is popular with tourists, to be used on a permanent basis.A planning report said the set provided a variety of exterior views and was used for more than 260 episodes each year.It said: "The Emmerdale Village Production Set provides a facility which adapts to the ever-changing needs of production."These could be planned changes for certain storylines or even immediate changes due to weather conditions, cast availability or other scheduling challenges."ITV said continued use of the set was needed to depict farming life and the Yorkshire countryside, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.Interior and exterior scenes were filmed at the Harewood site, while studio space on Kirkstall Road was used for some indoor sets, including the Woolpack.The report said: "Emmerdale Village was designed to include everything a typical rural village would have, including a village hall, café, church, residential dwellings and more."Current planning permission would expire on 3 June 2027, with a condition requiring the site to be restored to its original condition within six months.A full planning application is out for consultation until 13 August.

schema.headline: Emmerdale makers seek forever home for soap village in Leeds
